_comment: The clinic terminal, D119. Before this scene the whole beat was one press:
the player walked up to the computer, the engine's own Use prompt fired,
await_terminal released and the objective ticked. Nothing was read, nothing
was downloaded, and the records the objective is ABOUT never appeared.
This is a menu, and it is built out of nodes the engine already has rather
than a redscript UI (rule 1). Three pieces:
the hub        an attachToWorld choice node at the terminal - the same
machinery as scene_box.json and scene_courier_shard.json,
which are both confirmed working in game.
the bar        questProgressBar_NodeType, vanilla's own download bar. Its
single shipped use is q005_07_vip_apartment.scene: the
Konpeki suite copying the Relic. The same beat, so the same
node. It starts the bar and RETURNS - see wait_dl.
the notice     questWarningMessage_NodeType, the big centre-screen line.
Vanilla uses it two doors away in the same scene for
'WARNING: UNAUTHORIZED SCANNING'. A machine talking over
the HUD, which is exactly this register.
Only opt_download leaves the scene, so the hub cannot be dismissed into a
half-finished objective: walking away just leaves the prompt standing, the
way the case's does. The audit read is optional and loops back to the hub.

_attachToWorld: Relative to #ac_terminal_origin, which is the terminal prop's own floor
point. 1.4 m up is the screen: computer_1.ent's origin sits about 1.5 m
above its feet (see ac_terminal_pc's zOffset of 1.48 and the workspot
measurements behind it), so this lands the prompt on the display rather
than on the floor in front of the counter. Lower it here if it reads
high in game - the number is data for exactly that reason.
range 2 is the vanilla hub range used by every other hub in this mod.

options._comment: Optional, and gone once taken. A failing condition REMOVES an option rather than greying it out (OI-14), which is the wanted behaviour here: the audit line reads once, and a player who already read it sees a menu with one thing left to do.

nodes._comment: 6 seconds of bar. Long enough to feel like a transfer, short enough that nobody resents standing there; vanilla's Konpeki bar runs 28.85 s under a scripted conversation, which this beat has nothing to fill.

The wait, and the reason it has to exist: questProgressBar does not block. Without this section the bar would animate over a quest that had already granted the archive and closed the objective - the instant, unearned version of the beat. 6.4 s covers the bar's 6.0 with a little air.

Sets the fact FIRST, then shows the line: if the player is interrupted out of the scene between the two, the worst case is a missed notice rather than an option that can be farmed twice. ashcache_terminal_full_read had no setter anywhere until D119 - it was declared, documented as the completionist read, and dead.
